fix: Add a note on the back that 入り口 and 入口 are the same word, iriguchi, written with and without the り.
verdictReason: Facts hold (chapter-11 r-38e9cd1ffb95 入口 "Entrance" iriguchi and chapter-19 r-a1b4e92d7376 入り口 "Entrance" iriguchi both ship, both ttsText いりぐち) but it is not a finding. Reading rule 9 says one word in two spellings keeps one answer, and the preflight check that polices English collisions (src/audit/checks/reading.js, reading-distinct-english) deliberately passes two word cards with the same ttsText as "one word in two spellings, ぎんこう and 銀行, and are fine", which is why preflight is clean here. The identical Answer and Says lines are what tells the learner it is one word. The proposed fix cannot be applied: the reading template (src/deck/cardTemplates.js READING_TEMPLATES) renders Target, Answer, Says and audio only, and card-rules-reading says a reading card has nowhere to show a note.

claim: The romaji for 五分 fuses the number and its counter, against the deck's pinned counter-hyphen rule that the same unit follows for 十分.
evidence: Card r-8090dd787fc2 五分 "Five minutes", pronunciation "gofun"; card r-9dcb6ec62c8e 十分 "Ten minutes", pronunciation "jup-pun". src/translate/romajiStyle.js JA_COUNTER_HYPHEN_RULE: "A number and its counter are joined by a HYPHEN: jūni-nichi, shi-gatsu, go-ji ... ip-pon". The lint misses it because fun is not in JA_SAFE_COUNTER.
verdictReason: Verified in cards.json: r-8090dd787fc2 五分 pronunciation "gofun", ttsText ごふん; r-9dcb6ec62c8e 十分 in the same unit is "jup-pun", and chapter-16 writes 一分 "ip-pun" (r-ba5f63b12e2a) and 六分 "rop-pun" (r-ac36b226c034). JA_COUNTER_HYPHEN_RULE (src/translate/romajiStyle.js:30) requires a hyphen between a number and its counter (go-ji, ip-pon) and 分 is a counter, so "go-fun" is the pinned spelling. The lint cannot see it: JA_SAFE_COUNTER (line 42) is gatsu|nichi|nen|mai|satsu|sai|banme|jikan, no fun/pun, and preflight is clean on the card, so this is not already reported. Polish is right: the reading is correct, only the join is off. Context for the fixer, not a new finding: the kana deck (chapter-26) writes its five minute-counts fused the same way (ippun, kyūfun, jūkyūfun, jūroppun, jūyonpun), so whichever sweep fixes 五分 should settle the collection on one spelling.
